    29	    /// **W5-82 (Phase 4.5.D part 6):** intern a number-format string into
    30	    /// the workbook's `FormatTable` and emit `Op::RegisterFormat` to the
    31	    /// op log if (and only if) the call allocated a NEW id. Returns the
    32	    /// `FormatId`, which the caller can pass to [`set_cell_format`].
    33	    ///
    34	    /// Idempotent on repeated calls with the same string — the second
    35	    /// call returns the same id without emitting a duplicate op. This
    36	    /// keeps the op log compact and replay deterministic.
    37	    ///
    38	    /// Direct callers of `Workbook::formats_mut().intern()` bypass the
    39	    /// op log silently; that path is documented as low-level and intended
    40	    /// for the qbook loader + tests + engine-internal reconstruction.
    41	    pub fn intern_format(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<FormatId, RuntimeError> {
    42	        // Check whether the table already knows this string. If so, no
    43	        // new id is allocated and we MUST NOT emit `RegisterFormat`
    44	        // (idempotent path).
    45	        if let Some(existing) = self.workbook.formats().iter().find(|(_, t)| *t == s) {
    46	            return Ok(existing.0);
    47	        }
    48	        // New string — predict the id the table will allocate so we can
    49	        // emit the op BEFORE mutating (append-before-mutate ordering,
    50	        // matching set_name / set_value).
    51	        let id = FormatId(self.workbook.formats().next_custom_id());
    52	        if let Some(oplog) = self.oplog.as_deref_mut() {
    53	            oplog.append(Op::RegisterFormat {
    54	                id: id.0,
    55	                string: s.to_owned(),
    56	            })?;
    57	        }
    58	        let allocated = self.workbook.formats_mut().intern(s);
    59	        debug_assert_eq!(
    60	            allocated, id,
    61	            "FormatTable::intern allocated a different id than next_custom_id predicted"
    62	        );
    63	        Ok(allocated)
    64	    }

   532	- `docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-consolidated.md`
   533	
   534	No 5.2 commits land until the consolidated audit doc is signed
   535	off.
   536	
   537	## Post-audit decisions (2026-05-19)
   538	
   539	The parallel Codex + Opus audit (transcripts in `docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-1-{codex,opus,consolidated}.md`)
   540	closed the gating audit checkpoint. Decisions locked in:
   541	
   542	### D-1: Format-id wire format changes — `FormatId = { peer_id, counter }`
   543	
   544	**Status:** ⏳ PENDING — multi-day schema-breaking work; queued for next session.
   545	
   546	**Source:** Opus H-1 + Codex V4 (independent confirmations).
   547	
   548	The pre-audit design left format-id collision resolution as
   549	open question 5 ("Phase 5.3 may switch to UUID"). Audit
   550	verified the collision is a real bug: two peers concurrently
   551	calling `intern_format("X")` and `intern_format("Y")` both
   552	predict next-id N from the same workbook base, both emit
   553	`Op::RegisterFormat { id: N, string: <different> }`. Replay's
   554	`FormatTable::register_at` rejects the second with
   555	`FormatRejectedSource::IdCollision`. Result: replay fails
   556	deterministically rather than merging cleanly.
   557	
   558	**Resolution:** Phase 5.2 changes `FormatId` from `u32` to a
   559	tagged tuple:
   560	
   561	```rust
   562	pub enum FormatId {
   563	    Builtin(u32),        // Excel-canonical ids 0–163 (unchanged)
   564	    Custom(PeerId, u32), // Phase 5 custom ids: peer-id + per-peer counter
   565	}
   566	```
   567	
   568	Each peer's allocator increments only its own `Custom` counter;
   569	two peers can't collide. Built-in ids stay `u32` for round-trip
   570	with Excel's id space.
   571	
   572	**Schema impact:**
   573	- `Op::RegisterFormat.id`, `Op::SetCellFormat.id`,
   574	  `ql_storage::FormatId`, `Workbook::formats_mut().intern`
   575	  signature, `.qbook` envelope cell-format-id encoding, xlsx
   576	  `cellXfs` numFmtId mapping all change.
   577	- Wire-format bump: `WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION` increments.
   578	- Backwards compat: old `.qbook` files with `u32` ids load as
   579	  `FormatId::Builtin(n)` if `n ≤ 163` or
   580	  `FormatId::Custom(LegacyPeer, n - FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID)`
   581	  for migration. (Phase 5.2 designs the migration path.)
   582	
   583	**Why not UUID?** UUIDs are bigger (128-bit), opaque to humans,
   584	and don't carry the peer-of-origin information that
   585	collaboration tooling wants. The tagged tuple gives the same
   586	collision-freedom with better debuggability.
   587	
   588	### D-2: AddSheet name collision — auto-rename in 5.2
   589	
   590	**Status:** ✅ SHIPPED at commit `1ca19e2fa37` (2026-05-19) — `Op::AddSheet` replay handler now auto-renames to `<name>(2)`, `<name>(3)`, … on `SheetNameError::Duplicate` with `AUTO_RENAME_CEILING = 10_000`. `Empty` + `ReservedCharacter` still reject. Cross-ref `crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs`.
   591	
   592	**Source:** Opus H-3.

     1	//! Register parsed OOXML `<numFmt>` entries with the workbook's
     2	//! `FormatTable`.
     3	//!
     4	//! **W5-D-14d scope**: format-code registration only. Per-cell
     5	//! application (reading worksheet `<c r="A1" s="N">` and applying
     6	//! the format from `cellXfs[N].num_fmt_id`) requires worksheet XML
     7	//! parsing the engine doesn't yet do; deferred to a follow-up.
     8	//!
     9	//! The benefit of registering now (without per-cell application) is
    10	//! that the workbook's `FormatTable` correctly carries the user's
    11	//! custom format strings, so when per-cell wiring lands it can just
    12	//! `FormatId(N)` directly without re-allocating ids.
    13	
    14	use crate::error::XlsxError;
    15	use crate::read::styles_xml::StyleIndex;
    16	use ql_storage::{FormatId, Workbook};
    17	
    18	/// Register every custom `numFmtId` (≥ 164) from the parsed
    19	/// `StyleIndex` with the workbook's `FormatTable`. Reserved ids
    20	/// (0-163) are Excel built-ins handled by the `FormatTable` defaults
    21	/// — skipped here.
    22	///
    23	/// **Replay determinism**: uses `FormatTable::register_at` (not
    24	/// `intern`) so the imported id matches the OOXML id exactly. This
    25	/// is critical for round-trip — exporting back to xlsx writes the
    26	/// same numFmtId attribute we read.
    27	///
    28	/// Returns the count of custom formats registered.
    29	///
    30	/// # Errors
    31	///
    32	/// - `XlsxError::MalformedOoxml` if a registration collides with an
    33	///   existing entry under a different string — that indicates the
    34	///   xlsx has two `<numFmt>` entries claiming the same id with
    35	///   different format codes, which is malformed per OOXML spec.
    36	pub(crate) fn register_custom_formats(
    37	    workbook: &mut Workbook,
    38	    style_index: &StyleIndex,
    39	) -> Result<u64, XlsxError> {
    40	    let mut count: u64 = 0;
    41	    for entry in &style_index.num_fmts {
    42	        // Reserved 0-163 are Excel built-ins — skip; the FormatTable
    43	        // already has them.
    44	        if entry.num_fmt_id < ql_storage::FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID {
    45	            continue;
    46	        }
    47	        // **W5-D-PM-2 (megaudit Opus-B HIGH-1 closure):** reject
    48	        // attacker-controlled numFmtIds beyond Excel's plausible
    49	        // ceiling. Excel's legal numFmtId range tops out at ~32767;
    50	        // anything higher is either malformed or a hostile attempt
    51	        // to trigger the `FormatTable::register_at` arithmetic
    52	        // overflow at `format.rs:153` (`self.next_custom_id = id.0 + 1`
    53	        // panics on u32::MAX).
    54	        const MAX_PLAUSIBLE_NUMFMT_ID: u32 = u16::MAX as u32; // 65535
    55	        if entry.num_fmt_id > MAX_PLAUSIBLE_NUMFMT_ID {
    56	            return Err(XlsxError::MalformedOoxml {
    57	                part: "xl/styles.xml".to_string(),
    58	                message: format!(
    59	                    "numFmtId {} exceeds plausible ceiling {} (rejecting to \
    60	                     avoid FormatTable overflow)",
    61	                    entry.num_fmt_id, MAX_PLAUSIBLE_NUMFMT_ID
    62	                ),
    63	            });
    64	        }
    65	        let id = FormatId(entry.num_fmt_id);

    67	        // from LibreOffice / Google Sheets sometimes emit
    68	        // `<numFmt numFmtId="164" formatCode="General"/>` — a
    69	        // declaration at a custom id (≥ 164) whose format string
    70	        // already exists as a built-in (id 0 = "General"). Quantbook's
    71	        // `FormatTable::register_at` rejects this with
    72	        // `StringCollision`. The Excel behavior is to accept the
    73	        // redundant declaration (the cell using `s` with `numFmtId=164`
    74	        // still renders as General). We treat collisions where the
    75	        // existing string matches as idempotent no-ops; only TRUE
    76	        // string collisions at the same id still error.
    77	        match workbook.formats_mut().register_at(id, &entry.format_code) {
    78	            Ok(()) => {
    79	                count += 1;
    80	            }

    83	                // (typically a built-in). The OOXML file re-declares
    84	                // it at a custom id — semantically redundant but

    87	                let _ = existing_id;

     1	//! `OpLog` — Loro-backed append-only operation log.
     2	//!
     3	//! Phase 2A.3.a (2026-05-12): scaffolding-only API. The log stores ops as
     4	//! JSON-encoded strings inside a single Loro `LoroList` container named
     5	//! `"ops"`. Each `OpLog::append` call serializes the `Op`, pushes a string
     6	//! into the list, and commits the Loro doc.
     7	//!
     8	//! ## Why JSON-in-Loro
     9	//!
    10	//! Per Round 7 architectural lock T1-D05, Loro is reserved for the op log
    11	//! layer. Phase 2A.3.a aims for minimum viable scaffolding — full CRDT
    12	//! semantics (LoroMap-per-op with typed fields) is reserved for Phase 5+
    13	//! when inter-peer merging becomes load-bearing. The JSON layer is
    14	//! invisible to callers: they see typed `Op` values via `iter`.
    15	//!
    16	//! ## Persistence
    17	//!
    18	//! `export_bytes` produces a `Vec<u8>` via `ExportMode::Snapshot`. The
    19	//! resulting blob includes the full state plus history; suitable for
    20	//! `oplog.bin` on-disk persistence (Phase 2A.3.c).
    21	//!
    22	//! `import_bytes` reconstructs an `OpLog` from such a blob. The reader
    23	//! probes the `"ops"` LoroList; if absent (or the wrong shape), the
    24	//! import returns `OpLogError::SchemaMismatch`.

   106	    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Result<Op, OpLogError>> + '_ {

     2	//!
     3	//! **Tier D2 (2026-05-19) — Phase 4.12 Opus-C HIGH-3 closure:** this

     7	//! External callers that previously imported

     9	//! `ql_io::oplog_persistence::*` (re-exported at `ql_io::*`).
    10	//!
    11	//! Phase 2A.3.c (2026-05-12) — original `.qbook/` ↔ op-log persistence.
    12	//!
    13	//! Adds `oplog.bin` as a sidecar file inside the `.qbook/` directory. The
    14	//! sidecar is written by `save_workbook_with_oplog` using the closure-based
    15	//! extension hook `ql_io::save_workbook_extending`, so it rides the same
    16	//! atomic-rename protocol as the envelope + sheet JSONLs. Crash recovery
    17	//! works transparently — `oplog.bin` lives inside the backup directory
    18	//! alongside the rest and recovers via `recover_from_crashed_save`.
    19	//!
    20	//! ## Sidecar filename
    21	//!
    22	//! `oplog.bin` — binary `Loro::ExportMode::Snapshot` blob (per
    23	//! [`OpLog::export_bytes`]). Versioning is handled inside the Loro snapshot
    24	//! format; this layer is content-agnostic.
    25	//!
    26	//! ## Documented behavior
    27	//!
    28	//! - `save_workbook_with_oplog` writes BOTH the workbook AND `oplog.bin`.
    29	//!   Any previously-present `oplog.bin` in the target is overwritten.
    30	//! - `load_workbook_with_oplog` reads BOTH. If `oplog.bin` is missing,
    31	//!   returns [`PersistenceError::Qbook(QbookError::MissingFile {..})`] —
    32	//!   no silent fallback to an empty op log per the no-fallbacks rule.
    33	//! - The plain `ql_io::save_workbook` (no oplog parameter) DROPS any
    34	//!   existing `oplog.bin` in the target. Callers that want to keep history
    35	//!   MUST use `save_workbook_with_oplog`. Loud: pinned by the test
    36	//!   `save_workbook_drops_existing_oplog_bin`.
    37	//! - The plain `ql_io::load_workbook` ignores any `oplog.bin` that's
    38	//!   present (returns the workbook only). Forward-compatible: a v2 reader
    39	//!   without op-log support can still read a workbook saved with an op log.

    50	/// Filename used for the op-log sidecar inside a `.qbook/` directory.
    51	pub const OPLOG_FILENAME: &str = "oplog.bin";
    52	
    53	/// Combined error type for the persistence functions in this module. Wraps
    54	/// both [`QbookError`] (from the underlying workbook persistence) and
    55	/// [`OpLogError`] (from Loro snapshot encode/decode).
    56	#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    57	#[non_exhaustive]
    58	pub enum PersistenceError {
    59	    /// Workbook persistence layer error (I/O, schema, malformed cell, etc.).
    60	    #[error("workbook persistence error: {0}")]
    61	    Qbook(#[from] QbookError),
    62	
    63	    /// Op-log encode/decode error (Loro internal, serde_json, etc.).
    64	    #[error("op log error: {0}")]

    66	}

    68	/// Save a workbook AND its op log to `path` atomically. Both files land
    69	/// together via the `.qbook/` atomic-rename protocol — there's no window in
    70	/// which the workbook is updated but the op log isn't (or vice versa).
    71	///
    72	/// Overwrites any prior `oplog.bin` in the target.
    73	pub fn save_workbook_with_oplog(
    74	    wb: &Workbook,
    75	    oplog: &OpLog,
    76	    name: &str,
    77	    path: &Path,
    78	) -> Result<(), PersistenceError> {
    79	    // Export the Loro snapshot bytes FIRST. Failing here (e.g., a
    80	    // serde_json NaN/Inf rejection nested inside an Op::PutValue) surfaces
    81	    // before we touch the filesystem.
    82	    let bytes = oplog.export_bytes()?;
    83	
    84	    // Hand off to ql-io. The closure writes `oplog.bin` into the temp
    85	    // directory; the atomic rename then moves it into place with the rest
    86	    // of the workbook.
    87	    save_workbook_extending(wb, name, path, |temp_dir| {
    88	        fs::write(temp_dir.join(OPLOG_FILENAME), &bytes).map_err(QbookError::Io)
    89	    })?;
    90	    Ok(())
    91	}
    92	
    93	/// Load a workbook AND its op log from `path`. Both files must be present.
    94	///
    95	/// Errors:
    96	/// - [`PersistenceError::Qbook`] if the workbook itself fails to load
    97	///   (missing envelope, schema mismatch, malformed cell, etc.).
    98	/// - [`PersistenceError::Qbook(QbookError::MissingFile)`] specifically when
    99	///   `oplog.bin` is missing — the caller asked for the op log; surfacing
   100	///   the absence loudly is the no-fallbacks-rule answer.
   101	/// - [`PersistenceError::OpLog`] if `oplog.bin` is present but Loro can't
   102	///   decode it (corruption, version mismatch in the Loro snapshot format).
   103	pub fn load_workbook_with_oplog(path: &Path) -> Result<(Workbook, OpLog), PersistenceError> {
   104	    let wb = load_workbook(path)?;
   105	    let oplog_path = path.join(OPLOG_FILENAME);
   106	    if !oplog_path.is_file() {
   107	        return Err(PersistenceError::Qbook(QbookError::MissingFile {
   108	            file: oplog_path,
   109	        }));
   110	    }
   111	    let bytes = fs::read(&oplog_path).map_err(QbookError::Io)?;
   112	    let oplog = OpLog::import_bytes(&bytes)?;
   113	    Ok((wb, oplog))
   114	}

   300	    /// Export the log to a binary blob suitable for on-disk persistence.
   301	    /// Uses Loro's `ExportMode::Snapshot` — includes full state + history,
   302	    /// compressed.
   303	    pub fn export_bytes(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, OpLogError> {
   304	        Ok(self.doc.export(ExportMode::Snapshot)?)
   305	    }
   306	
   307	    /// Reconstruct an `OpLog` from a previously-exported snapshot.
   308	    /// If the snapshot doesn't carry our `"ops"` container shape,
   309	    /// subsequent `iter` / `len` calls operate on an empty list
   310	    /// (Loro creates absent root containers on first access).
   311	    pub fn import_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, OpLogError> {
   312	        let doc = LoroDoc::new();
   313	        doc.import(bytes)?;
   314	        Ok(Self { doc })
   315	    }
   316	
   317	    /// **Phase 5.2 D-4 (2026-05-19):** merge another peer's snapshot
   318	    /// into this log via Loro's CRDT merge. Concurrent appends to
   319	    /// the `"ops"` LoroList are preserved in deterministic causal
   320	    /// order (Fugue/origin-based with peer-id tiebreaker per
   321	    /// `loro-internal::container::richtext::tracker::crdt_rope`).
   322	    ///
   323	    /// Typical pattern for multi-peer collaboration:
   324	    /// 1. Both peers start from a shared snapshot (`import_bytes`).
   325	    /// 2. Each peer appends its own ops independently.
   326	    /// 3. Peer A exports its current state via `export_bytes`.
   327	    /// 4. Peer B calls `merge_bytes(&a_bytes)` — peer B's log now
   328	    ///    contains both peers' ops in causal order.
   329	    /// 5. Replay against a workbook reconstructs the merged state.
   330	    /// 6. `WorkbookRuntime::recompute_all` resolves derived state
   331	    ///    (spills, formula values) from the merged final state.

    23	    /// drift (older binary reading newer ops).
    24	    #[error("op log deserialize error at op index {index}: {source}")]
    25	    Deserialize {
    26	        index: usize,
    27	        #[source]
    28	        source: serde_json::Error,
    29	    },
    30	
    31	    /// Wrapped Loro internal error (commit / import / container access).
    32	    /// Surfaces through `#[from]` so call sites that use `?` get automatic
    33	    /// conversion.
    34	    #[error("op log loro error: {0}")]
    35	    Loro(#[from] loro::LoroError),
    36	
    37	    /// Wrapped Loro encode error (raised by `LoroDoc::export`). Distinct
    38	    /// from `LoroError` (decode) in Loro 1.12.0's API surface.
    39	    #[error("op log loro encode error: {0}")]
    40	    LoroEncode(#[from] loro::LoroEncodeError),
    41	
    42	    /// The op log's internal Loro shape doesn't match what we wrote. Fires
    43	    /// when an imported snapshot was produced by code that wrote a
    44	    /// different container layout (e.g., a future version of this crate).
    45	    #[error("op log schema mismatch: {0}")]
    46	    SchemaMismatch(&'static str),
    47	}

[MEDIUM] `FormatIdWire` silently accepts unknown fields inside variants  
File:Line: [wire.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/wire.rs:281)  
Detail: The serialized shape is correct, but the enum lacks `deny_unknown_fields`. A payload like `{"kind":"builtin","id":14,"counter":7}` will be accepted with `counter` ignored, which weakens the schema-version discipline for this new wire type. `Op` itself denies unknown fields, but that does not protect nested `FormatIdWire` variant payloads.  
Recommendation: fix now. Add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields, tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]` plus rejection tests for extra fields.

[LOW] Step-2 shipped doc still says commit pending

Detail: The checklist marks step 2 shipped, but the commit line still says `pending`. `crdt-data-model.md` can remain overall “implementation pending” for D-1, but the checklist should point at `135bbb99f75` now.  
Recommendation: defer to step 3 or the next doc touch.

PASS on the core wire shape. `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]` gives the tested JSON forms, and `PeerId` is `#[serde(transparent)]`, so `peer` is a raw `u64`. Field names `id`, `peer`, and `counter` stay as written.

PASS on `from_u32_legacy`. Storage’s actual boundary is `FIRST_CUSTOM_FORMAT_ID = 164` in [format.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs:29). `u32::MAX` maps without overflow to `Custom { peer: LEGACY_PEER, counter: 4294967131 }`; I’d add that exact boundary test, but I don’t see a correctness bug. TOML/serde will reject negative literals for old `u32` fields before this helper runs.

PASS/defer on collision freedom. The current test only proves distinct-peer equality/hash semantics, not allocator correctness. Same-peer duplicate prevention belongs in step 3’s `FormatTable::register_at` and per-peer allocator tests.

PASS on helpers. Don’t add `is_builtin` / `is_custom` until step 3 or 4 has a real use site.

PASS on step-4 readiness with one caution: migration is mechanical at `Op::RegisterFormat { id: u32 }` and `SetCellFormat { id: Option<u32> }`, plus replay/runtime sites. The producer must stop relying on a global numeric `next_custom_id()` and allocate under the local peer.

PASS on step-5 readiness. Current `.qbook` stores `FormatEntry.id` and `FormatOverlayEntry.id` as `u32`; step 5 must convert both `formats.entries[].id` and every `sheets.format_overlay[].id` via the legacy mapping.

PASS on const placement. Keep `FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX` private here; step 5 should call `from_u32_legacy`, not duplicate `163`. A public xlsx boundary constant belongs with storage/xlsx mapping, not `ql_oplog::wire`.

PASS on `Hash`. `PeerId` derives `Hash`, so `FormatIdWire`’s derived `Hash` is fine.

PASS on forward evolution. Lack of `#[non_exhaustive]` is consistent with the crate docs saying wire enums are exhaustive and variant additions are schema/version events. Step 7’s oplog header is still the right guard for old-reader rejection.

Verified: `cargo test -p ql-oplog format_id_wire` passes, 9/9.
